title: BOOKED FOR 7:13

title: WHITE BEAR’S COUSIN

title: NEW INFORMATION RECEIPT

title: SEVEN-WORD VERSION
jolly: Seven-word budget. Spend wisely.
cheeky: Your 40-minute loop just got a brutal word limit.
unfiltered: If the thought needs 800 words to stay huge, seven can puncture the damn balloon.

mind_bend: A loop often needs many words to keep feeling enormous.
loop: ↻ ONE MORE CLEAN PASS—THEN CLOSE THE TAB.

title: PUT IT ON THE WALL
jolly: Your wall has one new temporary tenant.
cheeky: Thought relocated. Rent remains unpaid.
unfiltered: Put the ridiculous sentence somewhere you can look away from.
mission: Your thought feels inside your head.
one_rule: Where in the room the thought would “sit” if it had to occupy a physical spot?

plot_twist: See if the thought becomes something you can look toward rather than something you are inside.
mind_bend: A thought can be something you notice, not a room you are trapped inside.
loop: ↻ SAME MENTAL MOVE? RUN ONE FRESH EXAMPLE.
safety: One planned pass is enough. If the thought returns later, reuse the trick once rather than repeating it until you feel certain.

title: STOP BEFORE THE LAST WORD
jolly: Tiny cliffhanger. No season finale.
cheeky: Your brain is furious about one missing word. Adorable.
unfiltered: That itch to finish the sentence is not proof the sentence matters.
mission: Your brain hates an unfinished sentence.
one_rule: How strong is the urge if you stop the loop one word early?
your_move: Begin the repeating sentence and deliberately stop before the final word. Hold the blank for five seconds. Don’t fill it.
plot_twist: Feel the pull to complete the phrase.
mind_bend: Sometimes the loop wants completion, not truth.
loop: ↻ FELT THE GLITCH? REPLAY ONCE—THEN OUT.
safety: One planned pass is enough. If the thought returns later, reuse the trick once rather than repeating it until you feel certain.
target_pattern: Need to finish a mental sentence

title: SEARCH BAR TEST
jolly: Search results: approximately zero useful pages.
cheeky: Your loop put on reading glasses and called itself research.
unfiltered: If no possible fact can answer it, stop pretending the dramatic loop is an investigation.
mission: Would you type this question into a search bar expecting one factual answer?
one_rule: The loop is actually asking for information or demanding impossible certainty — yes or no?
your_move: Turn the loop into a search query. Could an expert, experiment or search engine ever return a finite answer? If not: UNKNOWN.
plot_twist: Catch how many “why me / what if forever / how do I know for sure” questions have no finite lookup result.
mind_bend: Not every question is a research task. Some are uncertainty wearing glasses.
loop: ↻ SAME STUCK POINT? CHANGE THE FORMAT.
safety: One planned pass is enough. If the thought returns later, reuse the trick once rather than repeating it until you feel certain.
target_pattern: Treating existential uncertainty like searchable information

title: SHOELACE START
jolly: We tied one metaphorical shoelace. Marathon cancelled.
cheeky: Motivation was late, so we started without it.
unfiltered: Stop waiting for motivation to send a messy calendar invite.
mission: We are not “doing the task.”
one_rule: The tiniest physical start changes motivation even one point — yes or no?
your_move: Shrink the start until it’s almost silly: open file, put shoes on, touch the form. Do only that. Recheck motivation.
plot_twist: Look for any change after motion begins rather than before.
mind_bend: You may not need motivation to start; starting may be one way motivation gets made.
loop: ↻ START BUTTON STILL HEAVY? MAKE IT SILLY-SMALL.
safety: Use this for a small, reversible next step. Do not let momentum override pain, exhaustion, safety or consequences that need proper thought.
target_pattern: Waiting for motivation before starting

title: CROSS THE DOORWAY
jolly: Congratulations, you entered the loading zone.
cheeky: We tricked your body into arriving before your excuses.
unfiltered: Do not do the whole task. Just get your ass into the room where it happens.
mission: Move your body into the task zone before your brain holds another meeting.
one_rule: Crossing one physical boundary will make the task feel more real or more impossible — yes or no?
your_move: Pick the doorway, desk, kitchen, car, shower or room connected to the task. Cross into that space and stop. You are allowed to do nothing else.
plot_twist: Spot how the decision changes once your body has already changed context.
mind_bend: Sometimes the first decision is not “do it.” It is “stand where doing it happens.”
loop: ↻ MOVED 1%? BANK IT. NEXT BRICK ONLY.
safety: Use this for a small, reversible next step. Do not let momentum override pain, exhaustion, safety or consequences that need proper thought.
target_pattern: Decision paralysis before task contact

title: TWO-MINUTE DECOY
jolly: Two-minute free trial. Cancel anytime.
cheeky: Your brain thought it was signing a 12-month contract. Nope.
unfiltered: You only agreed to two noisy minutes, not a lifetime subscription.
mission: Offer your brain a deal so small it suspects a scam.
one_rule: Starting for only two minutes feels less threatening than “finish it” — yes or no?
your_move: Set two minutes. Work only until the timer. At the bell, stopping is genuinely allowed—even if momentum appears.
plot_twist: Catch the difference between resistance to the whole task and resistance after two minutes of contact.
mind_bend: Starting and finishing are different contracts. You only signed the first one.

safety: Use this for a small, reversible next step. Do not let momentum override pain, exhaustion, safety or consequences that need proper thought.

title: STEAL FRICTION FROM TOMORROW
jolly: Tiny burglary against future procrastination.
cheeky: Future-you just inherited fewer excuses.
unfiltered: Stop asking tomorrow-you for heroics. Remove one damn obstacle now.
mission: Do not do tomorrow’s task.
one_rule: Which tiny obstacle future-you is most likely to use as an excuse?
your_move: Remove exactly one friction point now: open the file, charge the device, put shoes by the door, place the form in the bag, fill the water bottle.
plot_twist: Spot that the future task is objectively smaller without any future motivation being required.
mind_bend: Make tomorrow easier instead of demanding that tomorrow-you be stronger.
loop: ↻ ENERGY LOW? LOWER THE ENTRY FEE.
safety: Use this for a small, reversible next step. Do not let momentum override pain, exhaustion, safety or consequences that need proper thought.
target_pattern: Expecting later motivation to overcome same obstacles

title: FIVE-SECOND CHOICE LOCK
jolly: Democracy briefly suspended for one snack-level decision.
cheeky: Five seconds. Pick a lane. You can change roads later.
unfiltered: It is reversible. Stop demanding a noisy prophecy before choosing.
mission: For one reversible choice, the parliament gets five seconds.
one_rule: Choosing quickly feels worse than continuing to hover — yes or no?
your_move: Pick a low-stakes reversible decision. Count 5–4–3–2–1. At one, choose A or B and physically begin it. No reopening for 60 sec.
plot_twist: Test whether discomfort comes from the choice itself or from losing the option to keep deliberating.

safety: Use this for a small, reversible next step. Do not let momentum override pain, exhaustion, safety or consequences that need proper thought.

title: UGLY FIRST BRICK
jolly: First brick: gloriously wonky.

mission: Make the first piece deliberately too ugly to judge you.

your_move: Make the worst acceptable first fragment on purpose: one clumsy sentence, rough first mark, messy name, badly placed object. Call it “brick 1.”

loop: ↻ STILL STUCK? MAKE THE NEXT MOVE SMALLER.
safety: Use this for a small, reversible next step. Do not let momentum override pain, exhaustion, safety or consequences that need proper thought.

title: MOTIVATION AFTER MOTION
jolly: Twenty seconds. Your motivation got fresh data.
cheeky: We stopped debating motivation and ran the tiny experiment.

mission: Let’s catch the order of operations instead of arguing about motivation.

your_move: Do exactly 20 sec of a real task. Stop. Rate motivation again—even if the score fell.

mission: Avoidance gives relief now and sends the invoice later.

your_move: Pin down the avoided action. Score “relief now” and “cost later.” Then imagine repeating the avoidance for seven days and score the weekly cost.

safety: Use this for a small, reversible next step. Do not let momentum override pain, exhaustion, safety or consequences that need proper thought.

title: SHRINK RAY
jolly: Tiny task achieved microscopic status. Perfect.
cheeky: We shrank the monster until it needed a microscope.
unfiltered: If the step is still scary, it is still too ridiculous big.
mission: Keep shrinking the task until resistance starts laughing.

plot_twist: Catch the exact size where “I can’t” becomes “well, obviously I can do that.”

title: NINETY-SECOND EXIT

cheeky: The task lost its “you live here now” clause.

safety: Use this for a small, reversible next step. Do not let momentum override pain, exhaustion, safety or consequences that need proper thought.

jolly: Option C is on annual leave.

plot_twist: Test whether mental noise drops when comparison space shrinks.
mind_bend: Sometimes freedom returns when you temporarily close a few doors.

safety: Use this for a small, reversible next step. Do not let momentum override pain, exhaustion, safety or consequences that need proper thought.

title: WALK THE FRICTION
jolly: Detective case solved: culprit was three extra clicks.
cheeky: Your motivation issue may have been hiding behind a dead charger.

loop: ↻ ENERGY LOW? LOWER THE ENTRY FEE.

cheeky: Why start a new engine when one is already moving?

mission: A routine already moving can carry one tiny passenger.

loop: ↻ SAME DELAY? CHANGE THE FIRST PHYSICAL MOVE.
safety: Use this for a small, reversible next step. Do not let momentum override pain, exhaustion, safety or consequences that need proper thought.

title: DONE IS A PLACE
jolly: Finish line installed. Tiny flag optional.
cheeky: “Work on it” finally got evicted.

safety: Use this for a small, reversible next step. Do not let momentum override pain, exhaustion, safety or consequences that need proper thought.

title: PROCRASTINATION COSTUME
jolly: Mystery costume reveal: it was discomfort all along.
cheeky: The task took off the mask. Underneath: one annoying feeling.
unfiltered: You may not hate the task. You may hate the noisy feeling at the entrance.

one_rule: Which feeling is hiding underneath: boredom, confusion, shame, uncertainty, resentment, fear of failure, fear of success?

loop: ↻ NO MOMENTUM? SHRINK THE START AGAIN.
safety: Use this for a small, reversible next step. Do not let momentum override pain, exhaustion, safety or consequences that need proper thought.
target_pattern: Task avoidance hiding emotion avoidance

title: EMOTION NEIGHBOUR TEST
jolly: Emotion postcode search: we are narrowing the suburb.
cheeky: “Bad” has been asked to provide a more specific address.
unfiltered: Your feeling deserves a better label than “everything is fucked.”

one_rule: Which pair is hardest to distinguish: angry/irritated, sad/disappointed, anxious/excited, guilty/ashamed, lonely/bored?
your_move: Pick the broad label you are using. Try two nearby alternatives. For each, finish: “If it were this, I would want to…”
plot_twist: See if different labels point toward different action urges.

loop: ↻ SAME SIGNAL, SAME STORY? TRY A NEIGHBOUR LABEL.
safety: Separate feeling, urge and choice. You do not have to suppress the emotion, and you do not have to act on it immediately.
target_pattern: Using broad label that obscures useful information

title: TWO TRUTHS, TWO HANDS
jolly: Two hands, two truths, zero cage match.
cheeky: Nobody has to win this round.
unfiltered: You can want it and fear it at the same sneaky time.

one_rule: Which hand feels heavier: “I want this” or “I’m scared of this”?
your_move: Hold one palm up for the want and the other for the fear. Say one honest sentence to each hand. Don’t force a winner.

mind_bend: Wanting something and fearing it can both be true without cancelling each other.
loop: ↻ 10% CLEARER? BANK IT. DON’T FORCE MORE.
safety: Separate feeling, urge and choice. You do not have to suppress the emotion, and you do not have to act on it immediately.
target_pattern: Belief conflicting feelings mean indecision or hypocrisy

title: ALARM / STORY SPLIT
jolly: Siren on one line, newsroom on the other.
cheeky: Your body rang the alarm. Your mind immediately wrote the press release.
unfiltered: The alarm is real. The story does not automatically get the same sneaky badge.
mission: Separate the siren from the news report.
one_rule: Which part arrives first: body alarm or explanatory story?
your_move: Say two lines only: “Alarm: ____” using body sensations. “Story: ____” using the meaning your mind adds. Keep them on separate lines.
plot_twist: Spot whether the story still feels identical to the alarm once they are visually separated.
mind_bend: The alarm can be real even when the story about the alarm is wrong.
loop: ↻ 10% LESS CERTAIN? BANK IT. STOP THERE.
safety: Use this to test added threat, not to ignore a real danger. Deal with concrete safety first, and do not repeat the ritual just to chase reassurance.
target_pattern: Body alarm fused with catastrophic explanation

title: FEELING GETS ONE VOTE
jolly: Three-person committee. Surprisingly civil.

loop: ↻ SAME PULL? MOVE VALUES ONE CENTIMETRE.
safety: Use the delay only for safe, non-urgent impulses. Real safety actions, basic needs and prescribed care come first.
target_pattern: Emotion treated as sole decision-maker

title: WHAT JOB IS ANGER DOING?
jolly: Anger has been asked to submit a position description.

jolly: Two hands, one tiny steering decision.
cheeky: Urge can complain from the passenger seat.
unfiltered: You do not have to kill the urge. Just stop handing it the overcooked keys.

title: EMOTION STICKY NOTE

title: SIXTY-SECOND PERMISSION

loop: ↻ 10% CLEARER? BANK IT. DON’T FORCE MORE.

title: NEON EXAMPLE / BORING CROWD

cheeky: Your worry rented the front row; the rest of the room kept existing.
unfiltered: The ridiculous world is bigger than your current line of sight.
mission: Your attention has been living mostly in front of your face.
one_rule: Three things you can know are behind you without turning.
your_move: Pin down what is behind, beside and above you from memory. Glance once to check one item.
plot_twist: Spot how awareness expands into space you were not visually monitoring.
mind_bend: The room keeps existing outside your current gaze.
loop: ↻ ONE MORE GENTLE PASS—NO STRAIN.
safety: Keep the sensory trick gentle and brief. Natural breathing only; stop if anything feels uncomfortable or more activating.
target_pattern: Near-body space overrepresented during stress

title: SOCK VANISHING ACT
jolly: Sock has briefly returned from invisibility.
cheeky: Your nervous system muted a perfectly real sensation for convenience.
unfiltered: Your brain edits boring overcooked signals out all day.
mission: Your clothes are touching you right now.
one_rule: Which clothing contact can you notice fastest?
your_move: Notice one constant contact—sock, waistband, sleeve, watch, chair. Hold attention there for five seconds, then let it go.
plot_twist: Catch how easily the sensation returns and fades again.
mind_bend: Not noticing something does not mean your body stopped sensing it.
loop: ↻ FOUND THE SWITCH? REPLAY ONCE.
safety: Keep the sensory trick gentle and brief. Natural breathing only; stop if anything feels uncomfortable or more activating.
target_pattern: Constant touch fading from awareness

title: WHITE PAPER TRICK
jolly: Your brain has been doing colour correction for free.
cheeky: Same “white,” different photons. Sneaky.
unfiltered: Perception is doing chaotic Photoshop before you even notice.
mission: Your brain keeps colours stable while light keeps changing.
one_rule: A white object looks exactly the same near a window and away from it — yes or no?
your_move: Pick a white or neutral object. Compare it under two different ordinary lighting areas without staring at bright sources.
plot_twist: Watch how your brain still calls both versions “white” despite different raw light.
mind_bend: What feels like a direct property can be a smart correction your brain is making.
loop: ↻ FELT THE SHIFT? REPLAY ONCE WITH A SAFE DETAIL.
safety: Keep the sensory trick gentle and brief. Natural breathing only; stop if anything feels uncomfortable or more activating.
target_pattern: Object colour perceived as stable across changing light

title: MICRO-SWAY CAMERA
jolly: Stillness caught fidgeting.
cheeky: Your body is balancing via tiny secret negotiations.
unfiltered: Even “still” is full of messy movement.
mission: Standing still is not actually still.
one_rule: If safe to stand, predict whether your body moves at all while you feel stationary.
your_move: Stand comfortably near support if needed, or sit upright. Notice tiny forward-back or side-to-side sway for 10 sec. Don’t correct it.
plot_twist: Catch movement that normally gets edited out of the idea of “still.”
mind_bend: Stillness can be made of constant tiny corrections.
loop: ↻ SAME SENSE, NEW DETAIL. RUN IT AGAIN.
safety: Keep the sensory trick gentle and brief. Natural breathing only; stop if anything feels uncomfortable or more activating.
target_pattern: Tiny movements occurring without conscious command

title: EYES CLOSED OBJECT CHECK
jolly: Eyes took a coffee break; fingers filed a report.
cheeky: Same object, surprise DLC.
unfiltered: Your eyes do not own the messy object.
mission: Your eyes may be bossing the object around.
one_rule: Use a safe familiar object. Call one detail your fingers will notice that your eyes ignored.
your_move: Close your eyes for five seconds while holding the object. Find one texture, edge or temperature detail. Open them again.
plot_twist: Spot whether the object feels newly detailed.
mind_bend: Reality gets richer when one sense stops monopolising the report.
loop: ↻ CAUGHT THE GLITCH? ONE QUIET REPLAY.
safety: Keep the sensory trick gentle and optional—no pain, bright lights, forced breathing or dizziness. Stop immediately if it feels uncomfortable or more activating. Only do eyes-closed steps while seated or safely stationary—never while driving, walking or moving.
target_pattern: Visual dominance overshadowing touch

title: INTERVAL CHECK
jolly: Three frames, tiny documentary.
cheeky: Your feeling failed to hold perfectly still for the camera.
unfiltered: Take snapshots; stop giving the messy sensation a livestream.
mission: We’re taking snapshots, not filming the whole feeling.
one_rule: The sensation will be identical across three ten-second-spaced checks — yes or no?
your_move: Check one body sensation now. Look away mentally for 10 sec. Check again. Repeat once more. Use only same / stronger / weaker / shifted.
plot_twist: Compare the three snapshots.
mind_bend: You do not need to watch a sensation constantly to discover that it moves.
loop: ↻ ATTENTION MOVED? BANK IT. TRY ONE MORE SAFE CUE.
safety: Keep the sensory trick gentle and brief. Natural breathing only; stop if anything feels uncomfortable or more activating.
target_pattern: A sensation assumed continuous when sampled intermittently

title: TURN THE ROOM
jolly: Room got remixed by a tiny head turn.
cheeky: Same world, different sensor angle.
unfiltered: Where you point the tiny sensors changes the tiny feed.
mission: Move only your head and the sensory world reorganises.
one_rule: Which direction contains the most sound or visual activity?
your_move: Slowly turn your head left, centre, right once. At each point, notice one different sound or visual detail. Keep the body still if comfortable.
plot_twist: Spot how changing orientation changes what becomes salient.
mind_bend: Sometimes “the world feels intense” includes where your sensors are pointed.
loop: ↻ SAME ROOM, DIFFERENT SIGNAL. RUN ONE MORE.
safety: Keep the sensory trick gentle and optional—no pain, bright lights, forced breathing or dizziness. Stop immediately if it feels uncomfortable or more activating.
target_pattern: Head direction shaping sensory field

title: TURN DOWN ONE WORD
jolly: One spicy word has been escorted out.
cheeky: The message kept its spine and lost a flamethrower.
unfiltered: Remove one ridiculous match before blaming the whole fire.
mission: Keep the point. Remove one degree of fire.
one_rule: Which single word is making the message hotter than the request?
your_move: Don’t send yet. Remove one loaded word—always, selfish, ridiculous, never, disrespectful. Read the same request once at half-speed.
plot_twist: Catch whether the boundary survives while the temperature drops.
mind_bend: Same boundary. Lower flame.
loop: ↻ VOICE STILL AT 100? LOWER ONE NOTCH.
safety: Lower the heat before you interpret, send, confront or decide. The point is not to erase the boundary; if you might act aggressively, create distance first.
target_pattern: One loaded word changing perceived hostility

title: SECRET CONTRACT
jolly: Secret contract located in the desk drawer.
cheeky: Apparently the other person missed the meeting where only you attended.
unfiltered: If the messy script matters, make sure both actors got it.
mission: They broke a script they may never have received.
one_rule: What exact behaviour did you expect without explicitly asking for it?
your_move: Finish: “I expected them to ___ because ___.” Then tag whether that expectation was stated, mutually understood, or private.
plot_twist: See if disappointment contains a hidden contract.
mind_bend: An invisible agreement is still invisible to the other person.
loop: ↻ SAME WEIGHT? LOOK FOR ONE POSSIBLE STEP.
safety: Do not force positivity, meaning or a fast recovery. Aim for a little space, movement or connection; stop if the exercise makes the weight worse.
target_pattern: Disappointment driven by an unspoken expected script

title: CURIOSITY VERSION
jolly: Question upgraded from courtroom to interview.
cheeky: Same issue, fewer handcuffs.
unfiltered: Ask the wild question without hiding the verdict inside it.
mission: Let’s see whether the sentence is trying to learn or trying to convict.
one_rule: How the other person would answer differently to an accusation versus a genuine question?
your_move: Take “Why did you ignore me?” and convert only the unknown part into curiosity: “What happened after I messaged?” Keep the issue intact.
plot_twist: Test whether the new wording leaves room for information you do not already possess.
mind_bend: Curiosity can protect your boundary while reopening access to facts.
loop: ↻ ONE MORE CLEAN SOCIAL CUT—THEN STOP.
safety: Use this to lower heat and reduce mind-reading, not to excuse harm. Keep drafts unsent while activated; boundaries and direct communication beat guessed motives.
target_pattern: Question phrased as accusation blocking information

title: TINY OLIVE BRANCH
jolly: Tiny branch spotted. Treaty optional.
cheeky: Peace offerings are sometimes embarrassingly small.
unfiltered: Do not let anger delete every wild sign of repair.
mission: Conflict brains are excellent at missing peace offerings.
one_rule: Did they make any small move toward normality, humour, help or contact after the tension?
your_move: Scan only for micro-repair attempts: a softer tone, practical help, meme, question, touch, ordinary comment. Don’t decide whether it was enough.
plot_twist: Spot whether the conflict story had filtered these moments out.
mind_bend: A tiny bid for reconnection can matter without erasing the problem.
loop: ↻ SAME SOCIAL STORY? TRY ONE MORE REAL ANGLE.
safety: Use this to lower heat and reduce mind-reading, not to excuse harm. Keep drafts unsent while activated; boundaries and direct communication beat guessed motives.
target_pattern: Small reconnection attempts ignored during conflict

title: REACTION RANGE
jolly: Future has been upgraded from one ending to three.
cheeky: Worst-case monopoly revoked.
unfiltered: Prepare for a sneaky range instead of rehearsing one sneaky disaster.
mission: Your brain picked the worst response and called it the only response.
one_rule: Three plausible reactions to the boundary: supportive, mixed, resistant.
your_move: Say 1 line per reaction. Name what you would do in each case without changing the boundary itself.
plot_twist: See if preparedness grows when the future has more than one branch.
mind_bend: You do not control their reaction; you can prepare for more than one.
loop: ↻ STILL READING MINDS? RETURN TO WHAT WAS OBSERVED.
safety: Use this to lower heat and reduce mind-reading, not to excuse harm. Keep drafts unsent while activated; boundaries and direct communication beat guessed motives.
target_pattern: Fear of a boundary based on imagined reaction

title: WRONG CHANNEL TEST
jolly: Your message may simply need more bandwidth.
cheeky: Maybe stop asking six text bubbles to perform a face-to-face job.
unfiltered: Use the tiny channel that can carry the tiny conversation.
mission: Maybe the conversation is hard because the channel is doing half the damage.
one_rule: The same message would land differently as text, voice or face-to-face — yes or no?
your_move: Grab the issue and imagine it in three channels: short text, phone/voice, in-person. Which parts need tone, speed, pauses or visual cues to be understood?
plot_twist: Test whether the problem includes a medium mismatch, not only a people problem.
mind_bend: Sometimes you do not need better words. You need a better pipe for the same words.
loop: ↻ POINT STILL FUZZY? SHRINK IT TO ONE EVENT.
safety: Use this to lower heat and reduce mind-reading, not to excuse harm. Keep drafts unsent while activated; boundaries and direct communication beat guessed motives.
target_pattern: Sensitive content forced into a poor communication medium

title: GIFT OR INVOICE?
jolly: Tiny accounting department activated.
cheeky: That favour may have had invisible payment terms.
unfiltered: Do not call it a gift if you are secretly sending a noisy invoice.
mission: Did you give something—or quietly issue an invoice?
one_rule: What did you expect back after your helpful act?
your_move: Pin down what you did for them. Finish two versions: “I chose to give this” and “I expected this to earn ___.” Notice which is more accurate.
plot_twist: Catch any hidden repayment term you never discussed.
mind_bend: A gift with an invisible repayment clause can feel like betrayal waiting to happen.
loop: ↻ SAME INTERACTION? CHANGE THE CAMERA ANGLE.
safety: Use this to lower heat and reduce mind-reading, not to excuse harm. Keep drafts unsent while activated; boundaries and direct communication beat guessed motives.
target_pattern: One generous act converted into a silent debt

title: MISSING FOOTNOTE
jolly: Footnote added; novel avoided.
cheeky: They may not be confused. They may simply be missing page 3.
unfiltered: Give them the stubborn context before judging their response to it.
mission: You may be reacting to a footnote they never received.
one_rule: One piece of background information your message assumes.
your_move: Read your sentence as if the other person knows only the literal words. Add the single missing context line that makes your reaction make sense.
plot_twist: See if the message becomes less mysterious or accusatory.
mind_bend: What feels obvious inside your history may be invisible outside it.
loop: ↻ 10% CLEARER? BANK IT. DON’T FORCE AGREEMENT.
safety: Use this to lower heat and reduce mind-reading, not to excuse harm. Keep drafts unsent while activated; boundaries and direct communication beat guessed motives.
target_pattern: Believing another person knows what you know

title: ONE PERSON GETS 60 SECONDS
jolly: One microphone. Revolutionary technology.
cheeky: Turns out two closing arguments are not a conversation.
unfiltered: Stop running two chaotic speeches at the same time.
mission: Two microphones are on.
one_rule: The conflict changes if only one person’s job is understanding for sixty seconds — yes or no?
your_move: Picture or practise a one-minute rule: person A explains; person B may only summarise, not defend. Switch later.
plot_twist: Spot how different “understand first” feels from “reply while listening.”
mind_bend: Being heard and being agreed with are different jobs.
loop: ↻ SAME ASSUMPTION? TEST ONE ALTERNATIVE.
safety: Use this to lower heat and reduce mind-reading, not to excuse harm. Keep drafts unsent while activated; boundaries and direct communication beat guessed motives.
target_pattern: Both people trying to be understood at the same time

title: DRAFT HAS A HALF-LIFE
jolly: First draft gets therapy, second draft gets Wi-Fi.
cheeky: Honest does not automatically mean sendable.
unfiltered: Write the wild fire. Send only what the relationship can use.
mission: Your first draft may be accurate to the feeling and terrible for the relationship.
one_rule: Which sentence will feel too hot after ten minutes?
your_move: Say the unsent version exactly as your emotion wants it. Tag it DRAFT. Copy only the factual point and request into a second version.
plot_twist: Compare emotional truth with communication usefulness.
mind_bend: Not every honest sentence needs a recipient.
loop: ↻ RELATIONSHIP STORY TOO BIG? ZOOM TO ONE MOMENT.
safety: Use this to lower heat and reduce mind-reading, not to excuse harm. Keep drafts unsent while activated; boundaries and direct communication beat guessed motives.
target_pattern: Draft emotion mistaken for send-ready communication

title: SAME SEAT TEST
jolly: Context loan approved.
cheeky: Funny how your own version came with footnotes.
unfiltered: Lend them one wild circumstance before diagnosing their whole character.
mission: Before you judge the driver, sit in the same traffic.
one_rule: What becomes plausible when you inherit their exact constraints for ten seconds?
your_move: Put yourself in their position: same time pressure, information, incentives and limits. Name one explanation that becomes possible from that seat.
plot_twist: Catch whether the character verdict loosens when the situation becomes concrete.
mind_bend: Character is easy to see when context is off-camera.
loop: ↻ ONE MORE CLEAN SOCIAL CUT—THEN STOP.
safety: Use this to lower heat and reduce mind-reading, not to excuse harm. Keep drafts unsent while activated; boundaries and direct communication beat guessed motives.
target_pattern: Your own behaviour gets context; theirs gets character

title: THE SCENE AFTER
jolly: Movie now includes the scene after the dramatic speech.
cheeky: Your forecast kept cutting to black at the worst bit.
unfiltered: Do not end the messy film at the hardest sentence.
mission: Your brain keeps filming the difficult middle and skipping the possible after.
one_rule: What the relationship looks like one hour after a calm honest conversation?
your_move: Picture three post-talk snapshots: relieved, unchanged, awkward-but-clear. Include ordinary details like making tea, returning to work, sending a normal message.
plot_twist: Test whether your forecast previously ended at the hardest sentence.
mind_bend: A difficult conversation has an after, not only a climax.
loop: ↻ SAME SOCIAL STORY? TRY ONE MORE REAL ANGLE.
safety: Use this to lower heat and reduce mind-reading, not to excuse harm. Keep drafts unsent while activated; boundaries and direct communication beat guessed motives.
target_pattern: Belief difficult conversations automatically damage connection

title: ANCHOR OBJECT
jolly: Tiny anchor deployed.
cheeky: A gap in contact is not the whole relationship database.
unfiltered: Put one damn stable fact next to the silence.
mission: Distance gets loud.
one_rule: One concrete sign of the relationship that exists even during silence.
your_move: Pin down one stable cue: shared plan, key, photo, routine, promise, past repair, scheduled catch-up. Hold only that fact beside the current uncertainty.
plot_twist: Spot whether the relationship feels less defined by the very latest contact.
mind_bend: Connection can have continuity even when contact has a gap.
loop: ↻ STILL READING MINDS? RETURN TO WHAT WAS OBSERVED.
safety: Use this to lower heat and reduce mind-reading, not to excuse harm. Keep drafts unsent while activated; boundaries and direct communication beat guessed motives.
target_pattern: Temporary distance interpreted without checking stable signs of connection

title: INTENTION IS PRIVATE DATA
jolly: Private server identified.
cheeky: They cannot read the file you never shared.
unfiltered: Your intention is private damn data until you communicate it.
mission: You know what you meant.
one_rule: Which part of your intention was actually observable?
your_move: Say two lines: PRIVATE INTENTION and VISIBLE BEHAVIOUR. Put the same interaction into both. Compare the gap.
plot_twist: See if “but I meant…” was asking them to access private data.
mind_bend: Good intent can be true and still need translation into observable repair.
loop: ↻ POINT STILL FUZZY? SHRINK IT TO ONE EVENT.
safety: Use this to lower heat and reduce mind-reading, not to excuse harm. Keep drafts unsent while activated; boundaries and direct communication beat guessed motives.
target_pattern: Your intention visible to you; only your behaviour visible to them

title: ONE ISSUE ROOM
jolly: Meeting capacity: one issue.
cheeky: Your argument had twelve browser tabs open.
unfiltered: Stop making one chaotic conversation carry the whole chaotic archive.
mission: Your current disagreement invited six retired arguments.
one_rule: The one issue that would remain if every older grievance had to wait outside.
your_move: Pin down today’s issue in 1 line. Each time an older example appears, label it OLD FILE and put it aside for a separate conversation.
plot_twist: Test whether the current problem becomes solvable when history stops crowding the room.
mind_bend: You can honour history without making every conflict carry all of it.
loop: ↻ SAME INTERACTION? CHANGE THE CAMERA ANGLE.
safety: Use this to lower heat and reduce mind-reading, not to excuse harm. Keep drafts unsent while activated; boundaries and direct communication beat guessed motives.
target_pattern: Old grievances recruited into a current argument

title: QUESTION BUDGET
jolly: Question printer has hit its daily limit.
cheeky: Your loop was running a subscription model.
unfiltered: You do not owe the chaotic worry unlimited questions.
mission: Your loop keeps minting questions faster than answers.
one_rule: How many new questions appear after you answer the current one?
your_move: Say the top question. Allow exactly one follow-up question. Any third question goes onto a parking name without answering.
plot_twist: Spot whether the loop’s power comes from question production rather than answer quality.
mind_bend: You do not need unlimited questions to prove you are thinking carefully.
loop: ↻ STILL STUCK? USE A FRESH EXAMPLE, NOT MORE FORCE.
safety: One planned pass is enough. If the thought returns later, reuse the trick once rather than repeating it until you feel certain.
target_pattern: One worry spawning endless new questions

title: SHUFFLE THREE SCENES
jolly: Editor has gone experimental.
cheeky: Same scenes, less destiny.
unfiltered: Shuffle the wild scenes and watch inevitability wobble.
mission: Same memory. Different edit order.
one_rule: The meaning changes if three moments are replayed out of sequence — yes or no?
your_move: Pick three snapshots from the event: before, peak, after. Replay them in the order after → before → peak.
plot_twist: Watch how inevitability weakens when chronology is scrambled.
mind_bend: A fixed sequence can feel like fate simply because it is the version you keep replaying.
loop: ↻ FELT THE SWITCH? TRY A DIFFERENT ITEM.
safety: Use this as one brief experiment with safe material. Do not drill distressing memories or keep testing until memory feels certain.
target_pattern: A memory feels inevitable because events are replayed in one fixed sequence

title: MOUTH CLOSED VERSION
jolly: Internal narrator has been put on mute.
cheeky: Apparently the thought needs subtitles to stay this detailed.
unfiltered: Stop giving the sneaky loop full voice-over.
mission: Let’s see what remains when the sentence cannot rehearse itself normally.
one_rule: The thought feels different if you stop mentally speaking every word — yes or no?
your_move: For 10 sec, hold only a rough image or single keyword for the worry. Don’t repeat the full sentence internally.
plot_twist: Test whether the loop loses detail, speed or authority.
mind_bend: A loop partly survives because language keeps rebuilding it.
loop: ↻ SAME PATTERN? CATCH IT EARLIER THIS TIME.
safety: One planned pass is enough. If the thought returns later, reuse the trick once rather than repeating it until you feel certain.
target_pattern: Exact wording maintained through inner speech

title: OUTSIDE DATA REQUIRED
jolly: Wrong database, excellent search effort.
cheeky: Your brain was refreshing a page it does not host.
unfiltered: Stop querying your damn head for data that lives outside it.
mission: This question may need data your brain does not possess.
one_rule: More thinking can actually generate the missing information — yes or no?
your_move: Pin down the unknown. Ask: “Would the answer require another person, future event, document, measurement or observation?” If yes, label OUTSIDE DATA.
plot_twist: Catch the absurdity of searching inside your head for data stored elsewhere.
mind_bend: Some uncertainty is not a puzzle. It is a waiting room.
loop: ↻ ONE MORE FRESH ANGLE—THEN STOP.
safety: Use this on a low-stakes, reversible problem. If more thinking is only making you more stuck or fatigued, stop and switch tasks.
target_pattern: Mind checking for an answer that cannot appear internally

title: SAME ENGINE, NEW PAINT
jolly: New colour, same noisy motor.
cheeky: Your loop changed costumes again.
unfiltered: Do not buy the ridiculous repaint as a new machine.
mission: Different sentence. Same engine?
one_rule: Today’s loop uses the same core move as yesterday: blame, prediction, replay, checking, explaining, comparing — yes or no?
your_move: Ignore the topic. Name only the mental action the loop performs. Compare it with one previous loop on another topic.
plot_twist: See if the subject changed while the engine stayed identical.
mind_bend: A new storyline can still be the same old machine.
loop: ↻ SAME MENTAL MOVE? RUN ONE FRESH EXAMPLE.
safety: One planned pass is enough. If the thought returns later, reuse the trick once rather than repeating it until you feel certain.
target_pattern: A recurring thought treated as fresh because content changes slightly

title: PUT A CLOCK OUTSIDE IT
jolly: Your epic saga may be 17 seconds long.
cheeky: Tiny runtime, impressive syndication deal.
unfiltered: Stop letting a wild 20-second loop lease the whole evening.
mission: Your memory loop has no clock.
one_rule: How many seconds the replay actually takes?
your_move: Start a timer and let one full loop run once. Stop when it repeats. Look at the number.
plot_twist: Compare the loop’s emotional size with its actual runtime.
mind_bend: A fifteen-second loop can rent half an hour if you keep renewing the lease.
loop: ↻ FELT THE GLITCH? REPLAY ONCE—THEN OUT.
safety: One planned pass is enough. If the thought returns later, reuse the trick once rather than repeating it until you feel certain.
target_pattern: Repeated replay missing actual elapsed time

title: CHECK THE CHECK
jolly: The check has been asked for a job description.
cheeky: Second inspection may be auditing your feelings, not the door.
unfiltered: Know whether you are checking the messy thing or checking your messy certainty.
mission: You checked the thing.
one_rule: What new external information a second check would add?
your_move: Before rechecking, state the first result and the exact new data you expect. If it’s only reassurance: FEELING CHECK.
plot_twist: Spot whether the target shifted from information to certainty.
mind_bend: A second look may be checking your anxiety, not the object.
loop: ↻ SAME STUCK POINT? CHANGE THE FORMAT.
safety: One planned pass is enough. If the thought returns later, reuse the trick once rather than repeating it until you feel certain.
target_pattern: Repeated checking for a feeling of certainty

title: DRAW THE PROBLEM BADLY
jolly: Art critics are banned from this experiment.
cheeky: Ugly diagram, surprisingly less tangled problem.
unfiltered: Stop feeding the bloody loop only words.
mission: Words keep circling.
one_rule: The loop changes when converted into shapes and arrows — yes or no?
your_move: Turn the problem into only circles, boxes and arrows in your head for 20 seconds. No sentences.
plot_twist: Spot which parts become simpler, missing or newly connected.
mind_bend: A thought can feel stuck partly because it keeps arriving in the same format.
loop: ↻ SAME ANSWER PATH? OPEN A SIDE DOOR.
safety: Use this on a low-stakes, reversible problem. If more thinking is only making you more stuck or fatigued, stop and switch tasks.

title: FIRST THREE WORDS
jolly: Launch code discovered. Missile not launched.

unfiltered: Catch the damn launch code before the whole loop boots.
mission: Your loop may have a launch code.

plot_twist: Watch the mind try to auto-complete the entire sequence.
mind_bend: Sometimes the first words are a button, not new information.
loop: ↻ STILL STUCK? USE A FRESH EXAMPLE, NOT MORE FORCE.
safety: One planned pass is enough. If the thought returns later, reuse the trick once rather than repeating it until you feel certain.

unfiltered: One chaotic event only gets one chaotic vote.
mission: The same evidence keeps walking back into court wearing different hats.

loop: ↻ BRAIN RELOADED IT? RUN THE TRICK ONCE.
safety: One planned pass is enough. If the thought returns later, reuse the trick once rather than repeating it until you feel certain.

jolly: Museum remains open, just not in your face.

mission: The loop may be getting notifications from its own museum.

loop: ↻ SAME PATTERN? CATCH IT EARLIER THIS TIME.
safety: One planned pass is enough. If the thought returns later, reuse the trick once rather than repeating it until you feel certain.

jolly: Reality accepted your rough draft.

jolly: Shop closed. Please return during actual business need.

your_move: Pick one review question only: lesson, repair, next action, or information needed. Answer it once. When answered, say REVIEW CLOSED.

loop: ↻ SAME MENTAL MOVE? RUN ONE FRESH EXAMPLE.

title: CEILING CAMERA REPLAY
jolly: Ceiling camera has zero emotional zoom.
cheeky: Your ego lost close-up privileges.
unfiltered: Move the damn camera and watch the story change size.

mind_bend: More time can create more work without creating more value.

cheeky: Same meeting, less internal fireworks.
unfiltered: A smaller stubborn reaction can mean the stubborn brain learned.
mission: The situation may not have changed.
one_rule: How reaction one compares with reaction five to the same safe repeated thing?
your_move: Pull up a harmless repeated experience—notification sound, first day route, routine meeting. Compare first exposure intensity with later exposures.
plot_twist: Spot whether repetition changed the reaction before it changed the stimulus.
mind_bend: A smaller reaction can be learning, not indifference.
loop: ↻ FEELING STILL FUSED TO ACTION? SPLIT THEM.
safety: Separate feeling, urge and choice. You do not have to suppress the emotion, and you do not have to act on it immediately.
target_pattern: Repeated safe exposure reducing response intensity even when the stimulus stays the same

title: TINY GOOD MOOD, BIGGER MENU
jolly: Tiny mood lift just added menu pages.
cheeky: One good song, suddenly more doors.
unfiltered: A little wild positive emotion can widen the wild menu.
mission: A small positive state can make the mind see more possible moves.
one_rule: How many ideas do you generate in a neutral state versus after a brief pleasant moment?
your_move: Use a harmless mood lift—favourite song, funny clip, pleasant view—then name five possible next actions for a stuck low-stakes problem.
plot_twist: See if the menu widens.
mind_bend: Feeling slightly better can change the size of the option space.
loop: ↻ SAME EMOTION? TRY ONE CLEANER DESCRIPTION.
safety: Separate feeling, urge and choice. You do not have to suppress the emotion, and you do not have to act on it immediately.
target_pattern: Mild positive emotion widening attention and available action ideas

title: LET A SMALL GOOD THING HELP THE BODY LAND
jolly: Stress stayed true; body found a softer runway.
cheeky: No toxic positivity. Just a nicer landing strip.
unfiltered: Let one chaotic good cue help the chaotic body come down.
mission: You do not need to become happy; sometimes a small positive cue helps the body come down.
one_rule: One gentle pleasant thing helps your body settle faster after mild stress — yes or no?
your_move: After an ordinary stressful moment, spend one minute with something mildly positive and safe—warm interaction, humour, nature, music—without denying the stress.
plot_twist: Test whether breathing, posture, or pace settles.
mind_bend: A small good feeling can coexist with a bad event and help the body settle.
loop: ↻ ONE MORE ALIGNMENT PASS—THEN CHOOSE.
safety: Separate feeling, urge and choice. You do not have to suppress the emotion, and you do not have to act on it immediately.
target_pattern: A mild positive state helping physiological recovery after negative arousal

title: ARE YOU CONNECTING OR REHEARSING?
jolly: Friendship stayed; endless replay lost automatic renewal.
cheeky: Good support, maybe too many reruns.
unfiltered: Keep the messy connection without replaying the messy problem forever.
mission: Problem talk can create intimacy and still keep the problem emotionally hot.
one_rule: The conversation produces a new action, new understanding, or mostly another lap — yes or no?
your_move: Pull up a repeated problem conversation. Tag what is CONNECTION and what is REHEARSAL. Decide whether the next conversation needs comfort, action, or a topic change.
plot_twist: Catch how closeness and rumination can coexist.
mind_bend: A conversation can feel supportive and still keep the wound rehearsed.
loop: ↻ SIGNAL STILL MESSY? RUN THE SPLIT ONCE MORE.
safety: Separate feeling, urge and choice. You do not have to suppress the emotion, and you do not have to act on it immediately.
target_pattern: Repeatedly analysing problems with another person increasing closeness while also keeping distress active

title: ARE YOU STAYING WORRIED TO AVOID THE DROP?
jolly: Worry has been caught selling shock insurance.
cheeky: Premium: all-day tension.
unfiltered: You may be paying messy worry to avoid a messy emotional drop.
mission: Staying tense can feel safer than relaxing and being shocked later.
one_rule: Calm feels risky because bad news would then hit harder — yes or no?
your_move: Picture two paths: worry all day then hear bad news, or get one calm hour first. Which transition feels scarier?
plot_twist: Catch the preference for steady discomfort over emotional contrast.
mind_bend: Constant tension can function like emotional shock insurance.
loop: ↻ BODY STILL ON ALERT? ONE QUIET PASS.
safety: Use this to test added threat, not to ignore a real danger. Deal with concrete safety first, and do not repeat the ritual just to chase reassurance.
target_pattern: Worry maintaining a steady negative state partly to avoid the emotional jolt of bad surprise

title: YOUR FEELING FORECAST JUST GOT NEW DATA
jolly: Emotional weather model just got field data.
cheeky: Forecast missed. Excellent—now learn something.
unfiltered: Use the noisy miss to update the noisy emotional model.
mission: The event is over.
one_rule: Intensity before one ordinary event, then rate actual intensity immediately after.
your_move: Calculate the emotional surprise: actual minus predicted. Keep the sign—better or worse than expected.
plot_twist: Test whether your future forecasting model deserves an update.
mind_bend: Every forecast miss is training data if you record it.
loop: ↻ SAME SIGNAL, SAME STORY? TRY A NEIGHBOUR LABEL.
safety: Separate feeling, urge and choice. You do not have to suppress the emotion, and you do not have to act on it immediately.
target_pattern: Unexpectedly good or bad emotional outcomes updating future expectations

title: CLOSE THE FORECAST LOOP
jolly: Emotional meteorologist finally keeps score.
cheeky: No more deleting the forecast after the weather arrives.
unfiltered: Score the messy forecast or it can stay messy wrong forever.
mission: Your brain makes emotional predictions constantly and rarely audits them.
one_rule: Pick one upcoming low-stakes feeling—dread, awkwardness, enjoyment, relief. Lock in 0–10.
your_move: After the event, score the actual number beside it. Keep both, without explaining away the miss.
plot_twist: Catch your personal forecasting pattern across repetitions.
mind_bend: A forecast that is never scored can stay confidently wrong forever.
loop: ↻ 10% CLEARER? BANK IT. DON’T FORCE MORE.
safety: Separate feeling, urge and choice. You do not have to suppress the emotion, and you do not have to act on it immediately.
target_pattern: Repeated emotional predictions staying inaccurate because actual outcomes are never compared back

title: BOX-IN-BOX ODDS
jolly: Story got richer; probability did not.
cheeky: Very convincing biography. Terrible set theory.
unfiltered: Do not let a overcooked detailed story outrank the overcooked larger set.
mission: A detailed story can sound richer while fitting inside a smaller probability box.
one_rule: Which box can contain more cases: A, or A plus an extra condition?
your_move: Picture A as a big box. Put A+B inside it as a smaller box. Now ask which box can possibly contain more cases.
plot_twist: Catch the story-feeling arguing with the nesting rule.
mind_bend: A story can gain detail while losing room to be true.
loop: ↻ SHIFTED 10%? BANK IT. OTHERWISE SWITCH TRICK.
safety: Use this to test the story, not dismiss real evidence or danger. One pass is enough; more checking is not more certainty.
target_pattern: A detailed combined story feeling more likely than one of its component events alone

title: CERTAINTY FLIPS THE PICK
jolly: Certainty just moved the furniture without changing the room much.
cheeky: Same contest, new probability costume, different winner.
unfiltered: Watch the messy certainty effect flip the messy choice.
mission: Two choices can preserve the same payoff difference and still flip your preference.
one_rule: Should adding the same extra chance of nothing to both options change your preference?
your_move: Compare: A = guaranteed $30; B = 80% chance $40. Imagine both receive the same additional 75% chance of nothing, leaving only scaled-down winning chances. Recheck preference.
plot_twist: Test whether the common change alters your appetite for certainty.
mind_bend: The options can stay almost the same while certainty changes how the choice feels.
loop: ↻ BRAIN RELOADED IT? RUN THE TEST ONCE.
safety: Use this to test the story, not dismiss real evidence or danger. One pass is enough; more checking is not more certainty.
target_pattern: Preference changing when identical probability mass is added to both risky options

title: BAD OUTCOME, FAKE MORAL CAUSE?
jolly: Bad luck has been denied automatic moral backstory.
cheeky: Terrible outcome, not necessarily a character review.
unfiltered: Do not make the tiny world feel fair by inventing tiny blame.
mission: When something unfair happens, the brain can try to make the world feel orderly by blaming the person.
one_rule: You would search harder for 'what they did wrong' after hearing the bad outcome first — yes or no?
your_move: Grab a harmless unlucky outcome. Name one thing you did, one situation factor, and one pure-chance factor before deciding what it means.
plot_twist: Spot whether moral explanation was appearing faster than causal evidence.
mind_bend: A fair world is comforting; inventing guilt does not make it fair.
loop: ↻ SAME PATTERN, NEW EXAMPLE. GO AGAIN.
safety: Use this to test the story, not dismiss real evidence or danger. One pass is enough; more checking is not more certainty.
target_pattern: A bad outcome creating an urge to invent a deservingness explanation

title: THE DOOR CREATED THE CORRELATION
jolly: Club admissions just invented a personality trade-off.
cheeky: The room did the correlation, not the people.
unfiltered: Check the messy doorway before believing the messy relationship.
mission: Two traits can look negatively related inside a selected group even when they are not related outside it.
one_rule: What happens if a club admits people who are either very funny OR very kind?
your_move: Picture the full population has independent humour and kindness. Now keep only people admitted for being high on at least one. Among members, compare the two traits.
plot_twist: Catch the selected group make high humour seem paired with lower kindness.
mind_bend: The room can manufacture a pattern just by deciding who gets through the door.
loop: ↻ ONE MORE ANGLE—THEN LET THE VERDICT REST.
safety: Use this to test the story, not dismiss real evidence or danger. One pass is enough; more checking is not more certainty.
target_pattern: Selecting cases because they meet at least one of two criteria creating a fake trade-off between those criteria

title: ONE PERCENT HAS A LOUD VOICE
jolly: One percent arrived with stadium speakers.
cheeky: Mathematically tiny, emotionally hired as headline.
unfiltered: Do not let messy possibility shout louder than the messy probability.
mission: Going from zero chance to tiny chance can feel much bigger than the maths says.
one_rule: Which change feels larger: 0%→1% or 40%→41%?
your_move: Say both as identical one-percentage-point changes. Notice which one changes your emotion more.
plot_twist: Catch 'possible at all' acting like a special category.
mind_bend: One percent can feel like a door opening, not just one point on a scale.
loop: ↻ SAME PATTERN? RUN THE TRICK ON A FRESH EXAMPLE.
safety: Use this to test the story, not dismiss real evidence or danger. One pass is enough; more checking is not more certainty.
target_pattern: A tiny chance of an outcome receiving disproportionate psychological weight

title: ASK THE OTHER HYPOTHESIS
jolly: Clue has been forced to interview both suspects.
cheeky: Fits your theory? Lovely. Does it fit the other one too?
unfiltered: Make the bloody clue discriminate before calling it bloody evidence.
mission: Evidence for your theory matters only if the rival theory would not predict it too.
one_rule: How often the same clue would appear if the alternative explanation were true?
your_move: Pick one piece of evidence. Say P(clue | your theory) and P(clue | alternative) in plain English, even without numbers.
plot_twist: Spot whether you had inspected only the first side.
mind_bend: A clue that both theories predict is lousy at choosing between them.
loop: ↻ STILL FEELS OBVIOUS? CHANGE THE LENS ONCE.
safety: Use this to test the story, not dismiss real evidence or danger. One pass is enough; more checking is not more certainty.
target_pattern: Judging evidence for one explanation without checking how often the same evidence occurs under alternatives

title: SAME GLASS, NEW LABEL
jolly: Math stayed home while wording changed clothes.
cheeky: Same glass, two marketing departments.
unfiltered: Make the sneaky complement visible before buying the sneaky frame.
mission: Ninety percent success and ten percent failure are mathematically married.
one_rule: Which description feels better before doing the subtraction?
your_move: Pick one statistic. Say both frames: X% succeed / Y% fail, X% lean / Y% fat, X% retained / Y% lost.
plot_twist: Spot the emotional change without numerical change.
mind_bend: The label can move the feeling while the quantity stays parked.
loop: ↻ CAUGHT THE GLITCH? TRY ONE CLEAN REPLAY.
safety: Use this to test the story, not dismiss real evidence or danger. One pass is enough; more checking is not more certainty.
target_pattern: The same attribute judged differently when described positively versus negatively

title: UNKNOWN ODDS FEEL WORSE
jolly: Unknown jar has been charged an uncertainty surcharge.
cheeky: Same prize, fuzzier odds, suddenly suspicious.
unfiltered: Do not confuse sneaky unknown odds with sneaky automatically worse odds.
mission: Your brain often charges uncertainty an extra fee.
one_rule: Which feels safer: a known 50% chance or an unknown chance somewhere around it?
your_move: Picture two jars: one has exactly 50 red/50 blue balls; the other has an unknown red-blue mix. Same prize for red. Notice your preference.
plot_twist: Catch dislike of unknown probability separate from dislike of risk itself.
mind_bend: Not knowing the odds can feel worse than bad odds.
loop: ↻ SAME CLAIM? GIVE IT ONE NEW ANGLE.
safety: Use this to test the story, not dismiss real evidence or danger. One pass is enough; more checking is not more certainty.
target_pattern: Known probabilities being preferred over unknown probabilities even when expected outcomes may be comparable

title: 100-POINT ODDS BUDGET
jolly: Probability budget has gone into overdraft.
cheeky: Every scenario got generous funding.
unfiltered: Do not let each wild possibility spend from a wild different wallet.
mission: Your sub-stories can quietly spend more probability than the whole story owns.
one_rule: Can your separate subevent estimates fit inside one 100-point budget?
your_move: Give the broad event 100 possible points. Allocate those points across the specific sub-cases without creating extra points.
plot_twist: Catch any urge to give the parts more probability than the containing event owns.
mind_bend: The suitcase cannot contain 140% of its own contents.
loop: ↻ SHIFTED 10%? BANK IT. OTHERWISE SWITCH TRICK.
safety: Use this to test the story, not dismiss real evidence or danger. One pass is enough; more checking is not more certainty.
target_pattern: Separate subevents receiving probabilities whose sum exceeds the broad event containing them

title: WHY ARE YOUR ODDS SPECIAL?
jolly: Your personal odds have been asked to show receipts.
cheeky: Apparently 'me' was getting a private insurance discount.
unfiltered: If your sneaky odds are better, make the sneaky evidence explain why.
mission: Average risk applies to everyone—until your brain reaches your own name.
one_rule: Your chance of one ordinary negative event, then predict the chance for a genuinely similar person.
your_move: Keep age, situation, habits and information as similar as possible. Compare the two numbers.
plot_twist: See if 'me' quietly received a discount.
mind_bend: Hope can be useful without secretly rewriting your denominator.
loop: ↻ BRAIN RELOADED IT? RUN THE TEST ONCE.
safety: Use this to test the story, not dismiss real evidence or danger. One pass is enough; more checking is not more certainty.
target_pattern: Estimating one's own chance of negative events as lower than comparable others without personal evidence

title: ENDING SWAP
jolly: Middle minutes have requested voting rights.
cheeky: Two dramatic moments were writing the whole review.
unfiltered: Do not let the bloody peak and bloody ending fire the whole middle.
mission: Change only the ending and watch the whole memory try to change its review.
one_rule: The same experience will feel different if only its final minute changes—yes or no?
your_move: Replay a recent harmless event once with its real ending. Replay the same event with a neutral final minute instead. Keep the middle unchanged.
plot_twist: Catch how much the overall verdict moves when only the ending is edited.
mind_bend: The last minute can become a critic for the whole movie.
loop: ↻ SAME PATTERN, NEW EXAMPLE. GO AGAIN.
safety: Use this to test the story, not dismiss real evidence or danger. One pass is enough; more checking is not more certainty.
target_pattern: A whole experience being judged disproportionately by its most intense moment and its ending

title: THE NUMBER NEEDED A NEIGHBOUR
jolly: Lonely number had no personality until a neighbour moved in.
cheeky: Seven became 'good' only after eight arrived.
unfiltered: Do not confuse chaotic comparability with chaotic importance.
mission: A number can feel meaningless until another number stands beside it.
one_rule: How good '7 defects' sounds without knowing what comparable products usually have?
your_move: Pick one unfamiliar attribute. Judge it alone, then add a plausible comparison value.
plot_twist: Catch how confidence and preference suddenly appear.
mind_bend: What seems important can depend on whether you know how to judge it.
loop: ↻ ONE MORE ANGLE—THEN LET THE VERDICT REST.
safety: Use this to test the story, not dismiss real evidence or danger. One pass is enough; more checking is not more certainty.
target_pattern: Attributes difficult to judge alone becoming influential only when comparison is available

title: THE FIRST THREE CAN STEER THE CROWD
jolly: Crowd may have started as three people and a domino.
cheeky: A hundred followers can inherit one early guess.
unfiltered: Write your tiny signal down before the tiny cascade starts.
mission: A crowd can become confident by copying itself.
one_rule: What would you choose if you could not see anyone else’s choice?
your_move: Grab a low-stakes rating or option. Say your private answer first, then imagine seeing three people choose the opposite before you respond publicly.
plot_twist: Spot the pressure to treat their choices as extra evidence.
mind_bend: A large crowd can grow from a very small informational root.
loop: ↻ SAME PATTERN? RUN THE TRICK ON A FRESH EXAMPLE.
safety: Use this to test the story, not dismiss real evidence or danger. One pass is enough; more checking is not more certainty.
target_pattern: Later judgments copying earlier visible choices despite private information pointing elsewhere

title: ONE BAD TRAIT GOT TOO MANY VOTES
jolly: One flaw has lost board-control rights.
cheeky: Bad haircut is not evidence of bad accounting.
unfiltered: Keep the ridiculous flaw out of ridiculous departments it never worked in.
mission: One thing you dislike can start reviewing everything else about the person or product.
one_rule: Which unrelated qualities do you rate lower after noticing one negative feature?
your_move: Pin down the disliked feature. Rate three unrelated dimensions separately using only evidence specific to each.
plot_twist: Catch the negative trait leaking into categories it did not earn.
mind_bend: One flaw can matter without becoming the whole evaluation system.
loop: ↻ STILL FEELS OBVIOUS? CHANGE THE LENS ONCE.
safety: Use this to test the story, not dismiss real evidence or danger. One pass is enough; more checking is not more certainty.
target_pattern: One salient negative trait contaminating judgments of unrelated qualities

title: THREE SOURCES OR ONE ECHO?
jolly: Three headlines just became one source wearing hats.
cheeky: Echo chamber submitted duplicate receipts.
unfiltered: Count the wild roots, not the wild copies.
mission: Three articles can feel like three confirmations even when they all copied the same source.
one_rule: How many independent evidence chains sit behind the claims you saw?
your_move: Trace each piece one step backward: original data, press release, same expert, same study, same rumour. Group echoes together.
plot_twist: Catch the evidence pile shrink when dependencies appear.
mind_bend: Repetition across channels is not the same as independent confirmation.
loop: ↻ CAUGHT THE GLITCH? TRY ONE CLEAN REPLAY.
safety: Use this to test the story, not dismiss real evidence or danger. One pass is enough; more checking is not more certainty.
target_pattern: Multiple correlated pieces of evidence feeling like multiple independent confirmations

title: WHICH VERSION IS JUDGING YOU?
jolly: Inner critic has finally shown its employee badge.
cheeky: Want-to and supposed-to just stopped sharing a desk.
unfiltered: Find out which tiny imaginary boss wrote the tiny standard.
mission: Not every inner critic works for the same boss.
one_rule: Which gap hurts more: who you want to be, or who you think you must be?
your_move: Say three lines: ACTUAL me now, IDEAL me, OUGHT me. Put the current complaint under the line that owns it.
plot_twist: See if desire and obligation feel different in the body.
mind_bend: A dream and a duty can sound identical until you name who issued the standard.
loop: ↻ LIFE STORY TOO BIG? ZOOM BACK TO THIS MOMENT.
safety: Use this to loosen pressure, not force meaning or positivity. Keep the conclusion provisional and tied to this situation.
target_pattern: Distress coming from confusing the actual self with ideal-self or ought-self standards

title: DID YOU STOP WANTING IT — OR LOSE ACCESS?
jolly: Closed door may have hired a critic.
cheeky: Amazing how quickly the grapes became 'overrated.'
unfiltered: Check whether the dramatic desire changed or the dramatic access did.
mission: Sometimes the desire changes suspiciously fast after the door closes.
one_rule: How attractive the option felt before it became unavailable?
your_move: Compare BEFORE BLOCKED and AFTER BLOCKED ratings. Imagine access suddenly reopened tomorrow.
plot_twist: Test whether devaluation protects you from the sting of not having it.
mind_bend: Not wanting something anymore can be wisdom—or emotional pain relief.
loop: ↻ 1% MORE SPACE? BANK IT. NO NEED TO SOLVE LIFE.
safety: Use this to loosen pressure, not force meaning or positivity. Keep the conclusion provisional and tied to this situation.
target_pattern: An unattainable option becoming less desirable after access is blocked

title: IF THE REWARD WASN'T ENOUGH, WHY DID I DO IT?
jolly: Tiny reward forced the mind to write a better story.
cheeky: One dollar apparently hired an internal PR team.
unfiltered: When the noisy excuse is weak, the noisy brain may rewrite the attitude.
mission: When the external excuse is tiny, the mind may rewrite the internal reason.
one_rule: How do you explain a boring task after a huge reward versus a trivial one?
your_move: Picture doing the same dull activity once for $100 and once for $1. Which version gives you more reason to tell yourself it was okay?
plot_twist: Catch the need for an internal explanation when the external one is weak.
mind_bend: Sometimes belief shifts because the obvious excuse was too small.
loop: ↻ SAME LABEL? TRY ONE FRESH VERSION.
safety: Use this to loosen pressure, not force meaning or positivity. Keep the conclusion provisional and tied to this situation.
target_pattern: Small external reasons producing more internal attitude change than large obvious rewards

title: ARE YOU LEARNING OR AUDITIONING?
jolly: Practice room has stopped pretending to be a talent show.
cheeky: Are we learning, or auditioning for imaginary judges?
unfiltered: Stop turning every tiny practice into a tiny courtroom for your ability.
mission: The same task feels very different when it becomes a talent test.
one_rule: What matters more right now: improving or looking competent?
your_move: Grab the task. Say LEARNING WIN and PERFORMANCE WIN separately. Choose which one you want this attempt to optimise.
plot_twist: See if fear changes when the audience leaves the goal.
mind_bend: A practice session becomes threatening when it is secretly an audition.
loop: ↻ PRESSURE RELOADED? SHRINK THE FRAME.
safety: Use this to loosen pressure, not force meaning or positivity. Keep the conclusion provisional and tied to this situation.

title: MISTAKE OR MEASUREMENT OF NOW?
jolly: Mistake has been denied access to your permanent record.
cheeky: Current score, not genetic prophecy.
unfiltered: Do not let one tiny miss write your tiny lifetime ceiling.
mission: One error can feel like a DNA test for ability.
one_rule: The same mistake would mean something different after ten more hours of practice — yes or no?
your_move: Say it again 'I am bad at this' as 'At my current training level, I missed ___.' Name the skill component that failed.

mind_bend: A mistake measures a moment more directly than it measures a lifetime ceiling.
loop: ↻ ONE MORE SMALL REFRAME—THEN LEAVE IT OPEN.
safety: Use this to loosen pressure, not force meaning or positivity. Keep the conclusion provisional and tied to this situation.

title: TRAIT OR CURRENT HABIT?
jolly: Trait label has discovered a settings menu.
cheeky: Apparently 'always' has office hours.
unfiltered: Find the damn conditions before calling the dramatic pattern permanent.
mission: Calling it a trait can freeze something that is partly a pattern.
one_rule: What evidence would show this characteristic changing across situations or years?
your_move: Pick one label—shy, impatient, messy, awkward. Find one context where it is weaker and one where it is stronger.
plot_twist: Catch how context variability challenges permanence.
mind_bend: A repeated pattern can be real without being immovable.
loop: ↻ SAME PRESSURE? TRY THE FRAME ON ONE SMALL EXAMPLE.
safety: Use this to loosen pressure, not force meaning or positivity. Keep the conclusion provisional and tied to this situation.

title: THE MEMORY KEPT THE STORY, LOST SOME STING
jolly: Memory kept the file and lowered the volume.
cheeky: Same story, fewer volts.
unfiltered: The tiny event can stay true while the tiny sting fades.
mission: Old bad memories can stay detailed while their emotional voltage quietly drops.
one_rule: How intense the event felt then versus how intense it feels to remember now?
your_move: Pick one ordinary past setback that is safe to revisit. Rate THEN intensity and NOW remembered intensity without rewriting the facts.
plot_twist: Spot what changed: event memory or emotional charge.
mind_bend: A memory can remain true after its original emotional volume changes.
loop: ↻ STORY STILL FIXED? LOOSEN ONE MORE NOTCH.
safety: Use this to loosen pressure, not force meaning or positivity. Keep the conclusion provisional and tied to this situation.

title: WHAT DID THIS EVENT CHANGE — EXACTLY?
jolly: Memory has been asked to show the bridge, not just the landmark.

mission: Not every important memory actually explains who you became.

title: UNCERTAINTY GETS A PARKING SPACE
jolly: Mystery has been given a waiting room instead of a forced confession.
cheeky: Relief is not evidence.
unfiltered: Do not marry a ridiculous answer just because uncertainty is ridiculous annoying.
mission: An unfinished question can feel so uncomfortable that any answer starts looking attractive.
one_rule: You want the answer because it is true—or because the uncertainty is exhausting — yes or no?

plot_twist: Spot whether uncertainty becomes bounded instead of bottomless.
mind_bend: An answer can feel relieving before it has earned the right to feel true.
loop: ↻ STILL CERTAIN IT ENDS BADLY? REPLAY THE EVIDENCE.
safety: Use this to test added threat, not to ignore a real danger. Deal with concrete safety first, and do not repeat the ritual just to chase reassurance.

title: WHAT KIND OF WIN IS THIS?
jolly: Goal nutrition label added.
cheeky: Same calories of effort, different psychological food.

mission: Two ambitious goals can ask for the same effort and feed very different parts of you.

your_move: Pick one goal and classify its main payoff. Imagine achieving it privately with nobody impressed.

loop: ↻ 1% MORE SPACE? BANK IT. NO NEED TO SOLVE LIFE.

title: CROSSED-HANDS TIME SCRAMBLE
jolly: One object just got a twin from finger geometry.
cheeky: Body map did some unauthorized duplication.
unfiltered: Your chaotic fingers crossed the chaotic coordinate system.
mission: Crossing the map can scramble which touch your brain thinks came first.
one_rule: Will touch order be harder to call with hands crossed than uncrossed?
your_move: With a trusted person, rest hands safely apart. Let them give two very light quick taps—one per hand. Call FIRST. Repeat once crossed, once uncrossed. Stop if uncomfortable.
plot_twist: Was the order easier to place when the body map was in its usual layout?
mind_bend: Even “first” can depend on where the body thinks its hands are.
loop: ↻ PERCEPTION JUST MOVED? CATCH IT AGAIN.
safety: Keep the sensory trick gentle and optional—no pain, bright lights, forced breathing or dizziness. Stop immediately if it feels uncomfortable or more activating.
target_pattern: Spatial body maps scrambling the perceived order of rapid touches

title: THE RING RESIZES THE CENTRE
jolly: Centre circle has been framed into a new size.
cheeky: Same circle, different landlord.
unfiltered: The overcooked ring can resize the overcooked centre without touching it.

title: ANGER BORROWS A GAVEL
jolly: Anger has been caught moonlighting as certainty.
cheeky: No new facts, much louder verdict.
unfiltered: Do not let damn anger lend its stubborn gavel to unrelated decisions.
mission: Anger can make unrelated judgments feel weirdly obvious.
one_rule: Which non-urgent decision suddenly feels 100% clear?
your_move: Do not decide it now. Rate certainty 0–100. Re-rate after the anger drops—same facts, no new research.
plot_twist: Catch whether confidence moves while evidence stays still.
mind_bend: Heat can borrow a gavel. It still is not evidence.
loop: ↻ STILL SEEING RED? COOL 10% MORE—THEN CHOOSE.
safety: Lower the heat before you interpret, send, confront or decide. The point is not to erase the boundary; if you might act aggressively, create distance first.
target_pattern: Incidental anger increasing certainty in an unrelated ambiguous judgment

title: FEAR ADDS QUESTION MARKS
jolly: Fear has been handing out extra question marks.
cheeky: One scary thing made the rest of the world look statistically suspicious.
unfiltered: Do not let one messy fear inflate every messy unrelated risk.
mission: Fear can make the whole world look less predictable, not the thing that scared you.
one_rule: Which unrelated choice seems riskier while you are frightened or keyed up?
your_move: Pick one ordinary unrelated probability judgment. Rate it now and later after the state settles without changing the evidence.
plot_twist: Catch the same risk feeling bigger when fear adds question marks.
mind_bend: A feeling about one threat can tint the probability of another.
loop: ↻ FEAR STILL OWNS THE SCREEN? WIDEN IT.
safety: Use this to test added threat, not to ignore a real danger. Deal with concrete safety first, and do not repeat the ritual just to chase reassurance.
target_pattern: Incidental fear increasing uncertainty and risk perception in an unrelated judgment

title: SADNESS CAN PRICE THE GAP
jolly: Sadness has been caught shopping for symbolic replacement.
cheeky: Loss feeling, unrelated cart.
unfiltered: Do not let the overcooked feeling of loss set the overcooked price.
mission: Sadness can make 'I need something different' feel unusually convincing.
one_rule: Does a purchase or life change feel more necessary when sad than when neutral?
your_move: For a non-urgent choice, say the price/value judgment now and revisit after the state changes.
plot_twist: Spot whether desire to acquire or replace moves without new information.
mind_bend: A feeling of loss can make unrelated acquisition feel like repair.
loop: ↻ STILL FLAT? TRY A DIFFERENT SMALL DOOR.
safety: Do not force positivity, meaning or a fast recovery. Aim for a little space, movement or connection; stop if the exercise makes the weight worse.
target_pattern: Incidental sadness increasing acquisition or replacement value in an unrelated choice

title: PAUSE THE GOOD THING ON PURPOSE
jolly: Good thing got a commercial break and came back visible.
cheeky: Turns out uninterrupted pleasure can become wallpaper.
unfiltered: Pause the damn nice thing long enough to overcooked notice it again.
mission: Continuous pleasure can fade into background.
one_rule: Your favourite song, snack, view, or show is more noticeable after a short interruption — yes or no?
your_move: During one ordinary pleasant activity, pause for 30 sec and return. Compare enjoyment before and after the break.
plot_twist: Catch attention renew on re-entry.
mind_bend: A small break can increase contact with something good instead of reducing it.
loop: ↻ SAME URGE? SEPARATE IT FROM THE CHOICE AGAIN.
safety: Separate feeling, urge and choice. You do not have to suppress the emotion, and you do not have to act on it immediately.
target_pattern: Continuous pleasant exposure fading into the background through adaptation

title: CAN'T CHANGE IT OR HAVEN'T TESTED A LEVER?
jolly: Whole emotion stayed employed; one department changed.
cheeky: Not total control. Still a lever.
unfiltered: Test one messy lever before declaring the messy whole system untouchable.
mission: The sentence 'nothing helps' can shut down experiments before they start.
one_rule: One part of the state you might influence without controlling the whole emotion.
your_move: Pick one lever only: body arousal, attention, interpretation, environment, action urge, social contact. Test it for two minutes.
plot_twist: Test whether any component moves even if the emotion stays.
mind_bend: You do not need total emotional control for one lever to work.
loop: ↻ FEELING STILL FUSED TO ACTION? SPLIT THEM.
safety: Separate feeling, urge and choice. You do not have to suppress the emotion, and you do not have to act on it immediately.
target_pattern: A global belief that nothing can influence an emotion reducing attempts to use specific strategies

title: STATE OR PROCESS?
jolly: Emotion has been converted from statue to weather system.
cheeky: Same feeling, now with a timeline.
unfiltered: Stop turning the damn feeling into a bloody permanent object.
mission: If you think feelings are fixed objects, you wait.
one_rule: How the sentence changes: 'I am anxious' versus 'anxiety is rising, falling, or holding right now'?
your_move: Turn one emotional noun into a process with a direction or time marker.
plot_twist: Spot whether the state gains edges and motion.
mind_bend: An emotion can be real and still be moving.
loop: ↻ SAME EMOTION? TRY ONE CLEANER DESCRIPTION.
safety: Separate feeling, urge and choice. You do not have to suppress the emotion, and you do not have to act on it immediately.
target_pattern: An emotion being represented as a fixed state rather than a changing process

title: PUT ORDINARY TUESDAY BACK IN THE FUTURE
jolly: Future event has been forced to share the calendar with laundry.
cheeky: Big event, still followed by breakfast.
unfiltered: Put the noisy ordinary day back into the noisy emotional forecast.
mission: Your forecast contains the event in HD and everyday life in invisible ink.
one_rule: What will you actually be doing three days after the outcome?
your_move: Keep the future event exactly as imagined. Add five ordinary activities that will coexist with it afterward.
plot_twist: Watch how the emotional future gains competing inputs.
mind_bend: The future event may remain important while ordinary life starts taking up space again.
loop: ↻ ONE MORE ALIGNMENT PASS—THEN CHOOSE.
safety: Separate feeling, urge and choice. You do not have to suppress the emotion, and you do not have to act on it immediately.
target_pattern: A future emotional forecast omitting ordinary activities that will compete for attention after the event
